Prevention: Early land preparation that includes clearing and burning of weed remnants immediately after crop harvest and early planting with effective rains of at least 30 mm cumulative
Intercropping maize with beans, cowpeas, soybeans to allow complete ground cover to provide shading effects on the weeds.
For intercropping plant maize at 90 cm
X 90cm, 3 plants per hill and plant legume seeds between maize stations
Use certified seed to avoid introduction through contamination
Construct contours and water ways to prevent runoff from an infested area
Discourage grazing animals in the fields to avoid spreading of seeds with animal dung
Monitoring: Tufted annual grass, spreading or stands straight, up to 40 cm tall.
Leaves bright green, flat or folded along central vein, up to 8 mm wide and 15 cm long.
Inflorescences with 3-8 'branches', each with two dense rows of flowers
Scout the fields weekly during the growing season looking for emerging weeds from crop emergence.
Consider direct control methods when the weed is found to be present
Direct Control: Weed as soon as weeds appear when it is young using a hand hoe.
If the weed is left to mature it is very difficult to remove without disturbing the crop
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
If there is a history of the weed use
Acetochlor (Acetochlor 900EC, Sprint 900EC) it is a pre-emergence herbicide.
Apply at a rate of 7.5 ml in a 15 litre tank immediately after sowing.
SC) is a post-emergence herbicide applied once the weed has germinated and before maize is sown.
Use at a rate of 23 ml in a 15 litre tank.
